Answer: A
Reason: The CT images (Figures 1a and 1b) demonstrate a large right pleural effusion and extensive mediastinal air/fluid collections (abscess) with an aorto-esophageal fistula, which corresponds to the progression described in option A. While Figure 2 shows a clear chest X-ray (likely the initial presentation before rupture), the definitive findings supporting the diagnosis on follow-up imaging are the massive right effusion and mediastinal pathology.
